---
title: "How to read fmrimod's evidence"
description: "A guide to the repository's checks, parity reports, caveats, and release receipts."
---

This page helps you decide what a green check or checked-in report actually
supports. It assumes you know the public workflow described in the
[golden-path tutorial](../tutorials/golden-path.qmd).

::: {.callout-note title="Scope of this page"}
The links below point to evidence committed in the repository. They do not
assert that the current checkout, the latest hosted workflow, a published
wheel, or a downstream project was verified while you read this page.
:::

## Four different questions require four kinds of evidence

| Evidence class | Question it answers | Strongest honest claim | It does not prove |
|---|---|---|---|
| Self-consistency | Do fmrimod objects agree with one another on controlled data? | The public path preserves its own design, fit, contrast, and metadata contracts. | Agreement with an independent implementation. |
| Numerical canary | Does one mathematical quantity match an oracle under tightly controlled inputs? | The named solver, contrast, transform, or statistic matches within the recorded tolerance. | That a user-facing workflow is complete or well designed. |
| Workflow parity | Does a realistic fmrimod path agree with a reference workflow? | The named path and comparator agree on the reported outputs, caveats, and inputs. | Coverage of untested workflows or a fully native authoring experience. |
| Flagship proof | Does a representative public workflow combine numerical evidence with inspectable semantics? | The named end-to-end family meets the checked-in numerical and interface criteria. | General release certification or universal parity. |

These classes are recorded in the
[`proof_artifacts.json` manifest](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/proof_artifacts.json)
and checked by
[`test_parity_proof_artifacts.py`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/tests/test_benchmarks/test_parity_proof_artifacts.py).
The classification matters: a precise low-level canary should not be presented
as an end-to-end user workflow.

## Read an artifact from the outside in

Start with the manifest row, then inspect four things:

1. **The workflow path.** It shows whether the fmrimod side uses the public
   seam, a private kernel, or an externally realized design.
2. **The report.** Check its status, metric values, tolerances, timing hardware,
   and recorded caveat identifiers.
3. **The reference path.** Confirm that the comparator is independent enough
   for the claim being made.
4. **The caveat index.** An accepted, bounded difference remains part of the
   result until its exit criterion is met.

Concrete examples:

- The public F-contrast case has a
  [workflow source](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/tier_a_f_confound_drift/public_workflow.py)
  and a
  [checked-in parity report](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/tier_a_f_confound_drift/reports_public/parity_report.json).
  It is workflow-parity evidence through `fmri_dataset → fmri_lm → contrast`.
- The SPM auditory case has a
  [flagship workflow](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/tier_a_spm_auditory/workflow.py)
  and
  [report](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/tier_a_spm_auditory/reports/parity_report.json).
  Its checked-in path authors the realized design in fmrimod.
- The semantic-survival case follows subject contrast intent into a
  `GroupDataset`; inspect its
  [workflow](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/tier_group_semantic_survival/workflow.py)
  and
  [report](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/tier_group_semantic_survival/reports/semantic_survival_report.json).

A self-consistency check remains useful even when it has no external
comparator. For example, the
[`first_trust_contrast` test](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/tests/test_examples/test_first_trust_contrast.py)
checks that a fitted contrast recovers a known injected effect and carries the
expected explanation. That supports internal trust in the path, not an
independent parity claim.

## FIAC is currently an interoperability bridge

The checked-in FIAC artifact reaches a public fmrimod fit and fixed-effects
combination, but its realized design comes from Nilearn:

`fmri_dataset → RealizedDesign(source="nilearn") → fmri_lm → combine_runs`

The
[`FIAC workflow`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/tier_a_fiac/workflow.py)
and
[`FIAC report`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/tier_a_fiac/reports/parity_report.json)
are valid workflow-parity evidence for that bridge. They are not evidence that
the FIAC design was authored natively from an fmrimod `Spec`. The
[`release_1_0_manifest.json`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/release_1_0_manifest.json)
therefore classifies FIAC as `interop_bridge`, not `native_flagship`.

## Caveats are part of the proof

The
[`CAVEATS.md` index](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/docs/contracts/CAVEATS.md)
records every active accepted divergence, its owner, affected tier, and exit
criterion. At present, it records the residual-degrees-of-freedom difference
for rank-deficient designs: fmrimod uses `n - rank(X)`, while the named Nilearn
comparison uses `n - p`. The row is not a waiver to ignore other differences.

When a caveat is closed, its evidence moves to
[`CAVEAT_RETIREMENTS.md`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/docs/contracts/CAVEAT_RETIREMENTS.md).
Each retirement names the old discrepancy, the resolving change, a proof
artifact, and a red check. Reading both files prevents an empty active index
from being mistaken for a project with no history of divergence.

## Release evidence is layered

| Layer | Repository evidence | What must still be checked |
|---|---|---|
| Declared release scope | [`release_1_0_manifest.json`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/release_1_0_manifest.json) classifies required families and public paths. | Whether those declarations match the intended release. |
| Checked-in bundle | [`release_receipt.json`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/release_1_0/release_receipt.json) records artifact presence, classifications, blockers, and regenerable commands. | Whether the receipt was regenerated from the current candidate. |
| Local candidate | The bundle generator and local test commands can rerun the evidence. | Whether the full supported environment and optional parity dependencies were available. |
| Hosted matrix | The [`release-0-8` workflow](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-0-8.yml) defines hosted Python 3.10 and 3.11 jobs. | The live run status and the exact commit tested. |
| Distributed release | Built wheels, indexes, and downstream installs provide external evidence. | Publication, installability, and consumer behavior for the exact artifact. |

The checked-in receipt reports no bundle blockers for its recorded input. That
is a structural receipt, not a claim that all later layers are green today.
The generator is
[`release_1_0_bundle.py`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/benchmarks/parity/release_1_0_bundle.py);
its tests are in
[`test_release_1_0_bundle.py`](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/tests/test_benchmarks/test_release_1_0_bundle.py).

## Continue from here

- Use [Troubleshooting](../help/troubleshooting.qmd) when a proof path skips or
  stops before producing evidence.
- Read [Group analysis](../tutorials/group-analysis.qmd) before evaluating a
  second-level result.
- For a fresh claim, rerun the artifact's recorded command and retain the
  report, environment, hardware tag, caveat state, and tested commit together.
